care_continuity: National isolation/CTE stock: 1130; provincial clinical scopes and missing reports remain explicit.
Ituri: 499 patients; printed occupancy 49.2; current source scope retained.
Nord-Kivu: 477 patients; printed occupancy 82.7; current source scope retained.
Haut-Uele: 35 patients; printed occupancy 19.0; current source scope retained.
Tshopo: 13 patients; printed occupancy 36.1; current source scope retained.
Bas-Uele: 106 patients; printed occupancy None; current source scope retained.
challenges: Contact follow-up is 25005/28067 (89.1%), below 95%; Ituri 86.2%, Nord-Kivu 92.5%, Haut-Uele 89.8%, Tshopo 81.4%, Bas-Uele 99.3%. Key messages identify Bambu 28.0%, Lita 50.8% and Gety 68.1% as critical.

451 suspects validated, 410 investigated (90.9%) and 261 transferred (63.7% of investigated). Forty-one remain uninvestigated: 26 Nord-Kivu, eight Haut-Uele and seven Ituri. None of 23 Bas-Uele suspects and only two of 18 Tshopo suspects was transferred.

Sixteen PoE/PoC alerts reported; six live alerts validated and five transferred. A confirmed-positive body intercepted at Foner Kasindi in public transport from Mutwanga was referred for safe burial. This is DRC operational context and does not establish a new international export. One traveller refused referral at Kangote; the Tshopo live alert was not validated. The table changes the strategic PoC/PoE row to counts without a percent denominator.

Ituri opened 25/41 rings, decontaminated 32/43 households, and performed 47/76 EDS (61.8%). Nord-Kivu opened 16/28 rings; only six of 19 households were decontaminated. A Tshopo household resists investigation, only six of 106 facilities exceed 80% IPC score. Bas-Uele reports two failed body swabs, 16 of 20 facilities lack functional triage and 17 lack a water point.

Ituri lacks blood, food for 20 Mandima patients and capacity at Aru, Mambasa, Kilo, Lolwa, Mandima and Biakato. Nord-Kivu has 163/192 suspect beds and 176/218 confirmed beds occupied; 138/477 patients are outside CTE/CT, intra-CTE mortality remains high and six zones have no ambulance. Haut-Uele has poor network coverage and the Pawa ambulance is under maintenance.

Ituri reports 1502 people vaccinated, 29 adverse events (three serious), and the TUMAINI trial planned for 23 October. In Haut-Uele, vaccination of frontline workers is halted; the Isiro generator failure prevents two cold-chain units starting. Bas-Uele cold-chain units are not operating and vaccines and funding remain insufficient. Nord-Kivu and Bas-Uele vaccination data did not arrive. No vaccine efficacy is inferred.

Recovery plans for Kyaghala and Katwa are unfinished; Komanda triage remains poorly functional. Tshopo child and maternity services have fallen. Haut-Uele has a deficit in free-care subsidies in the seven most affected zones and delayed catch-up vaccination.

Ituri psychosocial coverage remains 15/28 affected zones; 18/37 latest cases not supported, a denominator different from this edition daily cases. Nord-Kivu has gaps in ten affected zones and reinsertion resources are missing. Haut-Uele lacks mobility for psychosocial staff at Wamba/Boma Mangbetu, computer equipment, and nutritional kits for weaned infants at Pawa/Wamba.

Nord-Kivu received 496/650 expected community alerts (76.3%), resolved one of eight incidents (12.5%) and engaged 1842/4750 people (38.8%). Tshopo reports two incidents: an attack on response teams and a house fire involving a community engagement worker.

Insecurity persists in 17 health areas of Mambasa and Mandima; a decontamination team narrowly escaped an attack in Kitaviro. Threats continue in Bafwasende; a community engagement worker house was burned at Kenge. Haut-Uele lacks a backup generator, and Bas-Uele diesel stock remains exhausted.
